what_metro_recommended: Keep buildings off steep slopes and keep the slopes wooded: leave areas of 20%+ slope in a natural/wooded state, limit development on steep slopes and unstable soils, and tighten slope provisions in Metro ordinances.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified in this audit. NashvilleNext CCM (Vol3) codifies slope/Conservation (CO) policy language and Vol4 action #210 calls for hillside regulations above 15% slope, but adoption/enforcement outcomes were not traced from primary records.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 12 documents (1973-2017); implementation not independently established.
primary_source_citation: NEA_1973 p73; General_Plan_1980_2000 p191-279; NashvilleNext_Vol3_CCM_CI_CO_OS_T_2017 p12; Urban_Forestry_Landscape_Master_Plan_2016 p39
unresolved_gap: No audited primary source confirms current hillside-ordinance thresholds actually enacted or acreage of slopes kept wooded.

what_metro_recommended: Preserve the Highland Rim escarpment as a natural landscape: keep the escarpment and its oak-hickory hilltops generally in a natural state for scenic and ecological value.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. Recommendation originates chiefly in the 1973 NEA and the 1980-2000 General Plan; no audited record documents escarpment acreage protected.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified in 3 documents (NEA 1973, General Plan 1980-2000, Concept 2010); implementation not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source quantifies escarpment land actually protected or placed under natural-landscape designation.

what_metro_recommended: Keep sewers and urban services out of rural Rim land: do not extend water/sewer into Conservation-Nonurban/rural areas; tie service extension to low-density semirural patterns.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. NashvilleNext Vol4 actions (#323) and Vol2 Land Use call to apply Rural CCM policies and discourage sewer extension; actual utility-boundary decisions not traced.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 8 documents (1973-2026); implementation not independently established.
primary_source_citation: General_Plan_1980_2000 p191, p197, p264; NashvilleNext_Vol4_Actions p79; NashvilleNext_Vol2_Land_Use_Transportation_Infrastructure
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms where sewer service boundaries were actually held versus extended into rural Rim land.

what_metro_recommended: Keep rural land rural and low density: limit rural residential to low-density semirural patterns, reduce sprawl, and use agricultural overlays (e.g., Bells Bend/Pennington Bend).
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. NashvilleNext Rural T2 CCM policies state the intent; adoption of agricultural overlay districts not confirmed from audited records.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 7 documents; implementation not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms rural zoning densities retained or agricultural overlay districts enacted.

what_metro_recommended: Require conservation subdivisions that keep open space: enable/require clustered 'conservation subdivision by right' and sensitive-site techniques that set aside common open space.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. 2011 Open Space Plan sets a 'conservation subdivision by right ordinance by 2012' target and Vol4 action #182 references a 50% open-space conservation-subdivision ordinance; enactment not confirmed from audited records.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 8 documents; implementation (ordinance adoption) not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms a conservation-subdivision ordinance was actually adopted or its open-space yield.

what_metro_recommended: Protect existing trees on private land during development: adopt/strengthen a landscape and tree-protection ordinance, increase tree preservation during construction, and resource code inspection.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Partly evidenced in-corpus: the 2016 UFLMP recommends a dedicated landscape ordinance with tree protection and 2 dedicated inspectors; the 2023 UTC Assessment still recommends evaluating codes to increase preservation, implying the gap persisted. Enactment outcomes not traced.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 7 documents; the 2023 UTC re-recommendation suggests only partial implementation, but adoption not independently confirmed.
primary_source_citation: Urban_Forestry_Landscape_Master_Plan_2016 p30, p41; Urban_Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2023 p29; Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2010 p19
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms the private-land tree-protection ordinance provisions actually enacted.

what_metro_recommended: Hold the county's tree canopy, including large forested tracts: preserve and expand canopy, set canopy goals (UFLMP 65% transect targets), and credit canopy/conservation land in climate and stormwater plans.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Partly evidenced in-corpus: canopy was measured in the 2010 Tree Canopy Assessment and again in the 2023 UTC Assessment, so canopy monitoring occurred; whether canopy was actually held or expanded to the 65% transect targets is not established from audited pages (per-subarea baselines in UFLMP remain far below 65%).
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 8 documents; monitoring implemented, canopy-level attainment not independently established.
primary_source_citation: Urban_Forestry_Landscape_Master_Plan_2016 p8, p46-59; Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2010 p19; Urban_Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2023; Climate_Adaptation_Resilience_Plan_2024_Final p204
unresolved_gap: No audited source reports current county-wide canopy percentage versus the 65% transect targets.

what_metro_recommended: Buy and protect natural land on and around the Rim: continue acquiring/protecting large natural areas, rural and forested land, and land adjacent to parks for habitat.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. Plan to Play 2017 and the 2011 Open Space Plan set acquisition intents; actual acres acquired not traced from audited records.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 7 documents; implementation (acres acquired) not independently established.
primary_source_citation: Plan_to_Play_2017_Full_Plan p167, p178, p185; Nashville_Open_Space_Plan_2011; NEA_1973 p132
unresolved_gap: No audited source quantifies natural land actually acquired/protected on or around the Rim.

what_metro_recommended: Meet the conserved-land acreage goals: Open Space Plan targets (3,000 ac parkland in 10 yrs + 3,000 more by 2035; 22,000 ac total conserved by 2035) and Plan to Play level-of-service acreage needs.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Partly evidenced in-corpus: the Plan to Play 2026 Update and NashvilleNext Vol2 report interim conservation/parkland acreage (e.g., 11,000 ac 2011 baseline; 14,000 ac 2015; 21,000 ac 2021 target), indicating tracking against goals; attainment of the 2035 targets is not established.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation/targets verified across 5 documents; progress tracked, full attainment not independently established.
primary_source_citation: Nashville_Open_Space_Plan_2011 p11, p17; Plan_to_Play_2017_Full_Plan p27; Plan_to_Play_2026_Update p107-133; NashvilleNext_Vol2_Natural_Resources_Hazard_Adaptation p16
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms the 3,000/3,000/22,000-acre targets were met; 1 row (market value) is a cost estimate, not a goal.

what_metro_recommended: Keep the Open Space Fund replenished: make regular effort to replenish the Metro Open Space Fund (stated balance $5M in 2011) and leverage investments with other dollars.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. Only one record maps to this promise, and as written it states the 2011 balance rather than the replenish action.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified in 1 document (2011 Open Space Plan); implementation not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source reports Open Space Fund balances after 2011 or replenishment activity; single-record promise.

what_metro_recommended: Use conservation easements and transfer of development rights: promote conservation easements, land trusts, and a TDR program to protect open land.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. Multiple plans recommend easements/TDR; no audited record confirms a TDR program was established or easement acreage secured.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 5 documents; implementation not independently established.
primary_source_citation: Nashville_Open_Space_Plan_2011 p31-32; NashvilleNext_Vol3_CCM_CI_CO_OS_T_2017 p8; Urban_Forestry_Landscape_Master_Plan_2016 p40

what_metro_recommended: Join regional efforts to conserve upstream land: participate in regional land conservation for upstream watershed protection.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Not independently verified. Single NashvilleNext Vol4 action (#148); no audited record of regional participation outcomes.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified in 1 document (NashvilleNext Vol4 Actions); implementation not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source documents regional/upstream conservation partnerships actually undertaken; single-record promise.

what_metro_recommended: Designate and actively manage Metro's natural areas: implement a Natural Area Management Plan / Natural Resources Management Program and individual management plans per area.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Partly evidenced in-corpus: Plan to Play 2017 describes a Natural Resources Management Program and the 2026 Update revisits natural-area management, suggesting program activity; full designation/management status not established.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 3 documents; program referenced, completeness not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source confirms how many natural areas were designated and have active individual management plans.

what_metro_recommended: Run a funded urban forestry program and keep canopy studies current: fund urban forestry coordination, set/implement canopy (tree density) goals, and repeat canopy assessments.
what_metro_actually_implemented: Evidenced in-corpus: the 2026 Hazard Mitigation Plan states Metro Water Services coordinates urban forestry, manages the tree bank, and performs a canopy assessment every five years; canopy assessments exist for 2010 and 2023, confirming studies kept current.
status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 6 documents; an operating urban-forestry program and recurring canopy studies ARE evidenced in audited sources (strongest-supported group).
primary_source_citation: Hazard_Mitigation_Plan_2026_Final p222; Urban_Forestry_Landscape_Master_Plan_2016 p27; Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2010; Urban_Tree_Canopy_Assessment_2023
unresolved_gap: Audited sources confirm program existence and 2010/2023 assessments but do not confirm program funding levels or that every five-year cycle was met.

what_metro_recommended: Protect rare habitats and species: protect cedar glades, wetlands and aquatic habitat; buffer sensitive streams; and act on invasive pests (e.g., Emerald Ash Borer).

status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified across 6 documents; invasive-pest response referenced, habitat-protection outcomes not independently established.
unresolved_gap: No audited source quantifies cedar glades/wetlands protected or mitigation actually achieved.

status_supported_by_evidence: Recommendation verified in 2 documents; implementation not independently established.
